builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Concordat: Typed Sessions for LLM Agents
summary: Concordat replaces prompt-based behavioral rules with a runtime finite-state protocol that restricts tool availability and enforces approval workflows before side effects. It costs the implementation complexity of defining state machines and subclass contracts, plus runtime overhead of state tracking and token budget accounting. Adoption can fail if the protocol specification is incomplete, allowing actions in unintended states, or if legitimate edge-case workflows are blocked by overly rigid state transitions.
rationale: This provides deterministic enforcement of critical business rules without requiring model retraining or additional GPU resources, making it immediately deployable on constrained infrastructure to prevent costly unauthorized actions.
technique: Finite-State Protocol Enforcement for LLM Agents

claims.statement: Concordat replaces prompt-based behavioral rules with a runtime finite-state protocol that restricts tool availability and enforces approval workflows before side effects. It costs the implementation complexity of defining state machines and subclass contracts, plus runtime overhead of state tracking and token budget accounting. Adoption can fail if the protocol specification is incomplete, allowing actions in unintended states, or if legitimate edge-case workflows are blocked by overly rigid state transitions.

Eliminates all policy violations (unauthorized state changes) in tau-bench airline tasks (0/50 and 0/128 violations) compared to baseline rates of 13/50 (26%) and 29/128 (22.6%), with no significant loss in task success.
